conviction_note: Q3 2026 was a price-recovery quarter: China polysilicon spot rose more than 30%, from about RMB 32k/t in late July to RMB 43k/t by late September, against a Q2 ASP of $4.04/kg. Management said shipments kept picking up, and the closest analog (Q3 2025: ASP $4.19 to $5.80, volume 2.3x) traded more than 11% higher premarket. Against that, the Q4 setup is soft: industry inventory reached 572k t, futures sit about 20% under spot, only 2-3 producers are transacting, and Q1 and Q2 2026 were large EPS misses that fell 12% and 9%. So I lean mildly up (p_up 56) on a large absolute move of about 11, built from confirmed releases because the baseline history is unreliable. The impact_sum of +1.9 and the scaled +1.32 agree in sign and are close in size.
bar: EPS: Q3 2026 consensus loss per ADS of -$0.43 (Benzinga Q3'26E, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DQ/earnings, via search snippet; page 403) and -$0.48 (TipRanks, 3 analysts, https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/GB:0I74/earnings, via search snippet). The two sources roughly agree, so the EPS bar is about -$0.45. Revenue: disputed, Benzinga about $77.4M vs EarningsWhispers $139.5M (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/DQ), so findings that rest on revenue are capped small. There is no company guide for revenue or EPS, only production guidance of 40-45k MT for Q3 and 160-180k MT for FY2026 (https://finviz.com/news/383976/daqo-new-energy-announces-unaudited-second-quarter-2026-financial-results). print_vs_bar_pct is on EPS: I estimate a Q3 loss of roughly -$0.25 to -$0.45 per ADS, about -0.34 at the midpoint, or about 25% better than -$0.45, with low confidence because impairment and volume are unknown. History of the bar: Q2 2026 printed -$1.20 against -$0.28 to -$0.51 consensus.
positioning_check: Short interest was 4,399,192 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, down from a 5,049,013 peak on 2026-08-31 and up from 1.53M on 2026-01-15. That is about 6.5% of 67.67M shares outstanding, with 6.56 days to cover (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/dq/shortinterest, read 2026-10-26). Against the 20d average volume of 453k in the baseline it is roughly 9.7 days. A moderately crowded short that has started to cover. Skew_25d is -6.19 vol points: calls are bid over puts, and the baseline reads 'upside paid'. Put/call OI is 4.79, so open interest is put-heavy while the skew pays for upside. The ATM spread is 75% of mid, so the 12.2% event-implied move is indicative only. Spot $10.11 is 0.3% above the 52w low and 71.7% below the 52w high, down 7.25% over 20d. Market cap is about $690M against $1.92B of consolidated cash, short-term investments and deposits with no debt (Q2 release). Goldman Sachs downgraded to Sell with a $10 target on 2026-08-25 (https://www.streetinsider.com/rating_history.php?q=DQ), and the stock sits at that target.

findings.finding: China n-type polysilicon spot rose more than 30% during Q3 2026. n-type recharge averaged about RMB 32,000/t in the week of July 23-29 and RMB 43,000/t by Sept 17-23 and Sept 30, granular RMB 31,000 to 40,300/t. In Q2 the market traded at RMB 31-34/kg and Daqo realised an ASP of $4.04/kg against a cash cost of $4.57/kg. Converting a Q3 mix weighted to Aug-Sep (about RMB 38-40/kg incl. VAT, ex-VAT at about 7.1 RMB/USD) implies a Q3 ASP of roughly $4.7-5.0/kg, up 15-25% QoQ and at or above cash cost for the first time in 2026. Consensus EPS of about -$0.45 already assumes a much narrower loss than Q2's -$1.20; the open question is the size of the gross-margin swing on inventory written down at Q2 prices.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The closest analog is Q3 2025: ASP rose from $4.19 to $5.80/kg, sales volume went from 18,126 to 42,406 MT, and the net loss narrowed to $0.22/ADS (non-GAAP +$0.05). Shares rose more than 11% premarket (https://www.itiger.com/news/1120736188, 2025-10-27). The two most recent prints went the other way: Q1 2026 (2026-04-29) fell 11.85% on a falling ASP and about $99M of impairment, and Q2 2026 (2026-08-20 amc) fell 9.35% on a -$1.20 vs -$0.28 consensus miss.
findings.why_not_priced: DQ is 0.3% above its 52w low and down 7.25% over 20 days, so the tape has not credited a 30% rebound in the input price. Had the rebound been priced, the stock would have firmed off the lows over Aug-Sep alongside spot. The consensus EPS of -0.43/-0.48 does assume narrowing, so part of this sits in the bar. What is unpriced is the size of the margin swing on written-down inventory, which in Q3 2025 took the company to a non-GAAP profit.
findings.independence: Separate weekly series show the same path: Sept 28 silicon-branch data at RMB 43k/32k (https://news.10jqka.com.cn/20260928/c680289466.shtml) and Oct 21 Zhitong at RMB 43k/40.3k flat (https://wap.stockstar.com/detail/IG2026102100037768). The company itself said in the Aug 20 release that forward prices had rebounded more than 10% from the low. All are industry series, not a Daqo-level number, so this is a proxy confirmed only directionally by the company.

findings.finding: Q3 sales volume is likely well above Q2's 15,190 MT. In the Aug 20 release the CEO said polysilicon transaction and shipment volumes 'have continued to pick up in the third quarter', and the company has a large inventory to sell: H1 2026 production of about 87.1k t against sales of 19.7k t. At 25-35k MT and about $4.8/kg, Q3 revenue would be about $120-170M. That compares with consensus revenue of about $77.4M (Benzinga) or $139.5M (EarningsWhispers). Against that, industry inventory still rose from about 510k t at end-June to 572k t at end-September, which limits how much any producer destocked.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume carried the Q3 2025 analog (+134% QoQ sales, more than +11% premarket). Q2 2026 revenue beat ($62.7M vs $59.2M) but EPS missed and the stock fell 9.35%, so a revenue beat alone has not paid.
findings.why_not_priced: The revenue bar is split by nearly 2x across aggregators, so no single number is priced. If $130M+ of revenue were expected, the low Benzinga figure would have been revised and the stock would not be at the 52w low.
findings.independence: H1 production and sales figures come from Xinjiang Daqo's Sept IR record (https://wap.stockstar.com/detail/IG2026100800019409, 2026-10-08), and the CEO comment from the TradingKey call transcript (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262122110-tradingkey). Counterweight on industry destocking: the Oct 17 Securities Times report of 572k t inventory (https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610173898786188.html). Capped small because the revenue bar is disputed.

findings.finding: The Q4 outlook the call will be asked about is soft. Industry inventory reached about 572k t at end-September and is expected to keep building in October. Industry utilisation is set to fall to about 35%, with October output down about 13% MoM and 6 producers cutting. Polysilicon futures were RMB 34,285/t on Oct 16 against RMB 43,000/t spot, about 20% lower, so the futures market does not believe spot will hold. Only 2-3 companies transacted in the week to Oct 21, and buyers are waiting. Daqo told investors on Oct 8-9 that it will set production according to supply and demand, which makes a Q4 production guide below Q3's 40-45k MT likely, with higher unit fixed cost.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Daqo gives production guidance only (no revenue or EPS guide). The Q2 release guided Q3 production at 40-45k MT, and the stock fell 9.35% on that print, though mainly on the EPS miss. No clean history of a production-guide cut moving the stock in the sources found.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock at its 52w low may already reflect industry doubt. What is not priced is Daqo's own Q4 production number and its comment on Q4 pricing and volume, which only the call delivers. Futures already sit 20% below spot, which is why this is small.
findings.independence: The Oct 21 weekly from the Silicon Industry Branch via Zhitong (https://wap.stockstar.com/detail/IG2026102100037768) reports thin transactions and buyers held back by the futures-spot gap. Daqo's IR remarks on production pace are reported by Caiwen (https://www.caiwennews.com/article/1643057.shtml, 2026-10-09). Industry-level evidence. Shrunk because of a 6.5%, 6.6-day short and call-bid skew.

findings.finding: The price floor partly offsets the Q4 risk above. On Oct 11, 2026 leading producers including Tongwei and GCL agreed that the tax-inclusive average sales price would not fall below RMB 43,000/t. That is today's rod spot, and it includes industrial silicon, power, depreciation and labour. Daqo signed the Aug 6 no-below-cost-sales pledge with seven peers, and SAMR issued price-compliance guidance on July 31. This supports Q4 ASP at or above Q3's exit level if it holds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Policy news has moved DQ sharply before (the July 2025 supply-side headlines; Citi Buy, intraday +6.6% to +17% per Tiger news archive), but those are not earnings-day reactions. No print-day history on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and the futures discount shows the market doubts it, so most of it is priced. What can move is management confirming on the call that its Q4 contracts clear at or above the floor.
findings.independence: The Aug 6 pledge and the July 2 energy-consumption standard (effective 2027-01-01) are confirmed in Daqo's own Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/383976/daqo-new-energy-announces-unaudited-second-quarter-2026-financial-results). Shares the Oct 13 document with finding 1 for the price levels, but this finding is about the floor and not the Q3 price.

findings.finding: Positioning leans toward an upside squeeze. Short interest is 4.40M shares (2026-09-30 settlement), about 6.5% of the 67.67M shares outstanding, with 6.56 days to cover (about 9.7 on the 20d average volume of 453k). It roughly tripled from 1.53M in January to a 5.05M peak on Aug 31 and has eased since. Spot $10.11 sits at the 52w low and at Goldman's $10 Sell target. Market cap is about $690M against $1.92B of consolidated cash and deposits with zero debt.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No squeeze has been documented on a DQ print in the sources found. Q3 2025, when shorts were about 4.3% of float, saw more than +11% premarket on a recovery quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is a published figure, but the asymmetry is not in the option price: the straddle is too wide (spread 75% of mid) to read precisely, and calls are bid by 6.2 vol points. If the squeeze risk were priced away, the skew would be flat and short interest would have fallen back to January levels.
findings.independence: The baseline skew_25d of -6.19 (calls paid) points the same way, from separate options data. The cash figure comes from the Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/383976/daqo-new-energy-announces-unaudited-second-quarter-2026-financial-results).

findings.finding: Inventory impairment risk persists into Q3. Q2 total production cost was $5.95/kg, including depreciation. The Sept-end spot of RMB 43k/t is about $5.3/kg ex-VAT, so Q3-produced inventory left unsold at quarter end probably still needs a write-down. Production of 40-45k MT against likely sales below that implies continued builds. Impairments of $98.9M in Q1 and $55.7M in Q2 caused both 2026 EPS misses (Q2 -$1.20 against a -$0.28 to -$0.51 consensus), so a third miss on impairment is possible even with better ASPs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Both 2026 prints with large impairments fell: Q1 by 11.85% and Q2 by 9.35%. Roth cut its target from $25 to $19 after Q1 on the ASP and an impairment of nearly $100M (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/daqo-energy-corp-dq-under-095543619.html, 2026-05-03).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of -0.43/-0.48 has missed by $0.7-0.9 in each 2026 quarter, so the estimate does not model impairments well. If the street expected another write-down, consensus would sit nearer -$0.8. The size of the impairment is my inference from cost versus spot, not a company figure.
findings.independence: Q1 and Q2 impairments are also reported in A-share terms in Xinjiang Daqo's IR: H1 impairment RMB 1.026bn (https://wap.stockstar.com/detail/IG2026100800019409). This rests on the same price data as finding 1 and runs in the opposite direction on the same line, so finding 1 is sized net of it. Shrunk for the crowded short.

findings.finding: A $100M ADS/ordinary share repurchase authorisation approved on 2025-08-26 runs to 2026-12-31, and no repurchase use was reported in the Q2 2026 release. The stock trades at about $690M market cap against $1.92B of consolidated liquidity, so an announced use, extension or new program on the call is possible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July 2024 $100M buyback announcement lifted DQ premarket (https://benzinga.com/markets/equities/24/07/39880921/why-polysilicon-company-daqo-new-energys-shares-are-trading-higher-premarket-today). No print-day history.
findings.why_not_priced: The program is public, but the company has not shown it is using it while cash burns. If the market expected use at these levels, the discount to net cash would be smaller. Any new action is speculative.

findings.finding: The AIDC power-equipment diversification (energy storage, solid-state transformers and breakers via a Kunshan entity) is still at the 'preliminary approvals' stage according to the Sept IR record published 2026-10-08, with first products expected by 2027. No revenue contribution in Q3 and no near-term catalyst.
findings.why_not_priced: It is known and immaterial to Q3. Filed so judges can see it was checked.
findings.independence: Pacific Securities 2026-09-22 note frames AIDC as a 'second growth pillar' (https://stock.10jqka.com.cn/20260922/c680161137.shtml).

baseline_tension: The lean agrees with the skew (-6.19, calls paid) and cuts against the 20-day run-up of -7.25% and the 52w-low tape. The tape says the market disbelieves the price recovery; my positive findings assume the Q3 numbers show it. The two 2026 EPS misses on impairment are why p_up stays at 56 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (proxy vs company number): finding 1 rests on industry spot series that the company has confirmed only directionally, so it moved from +2.0 to +1.5.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the EPS bar is two roughly agreeing sources (-0.43/-0.48) but the revenue bar is disputed ($77M vs $140M), so the revenue/volume finding 2 is capped from +1.0 to +0.6.
Lesson 7 (positioning): the negatives face 6.5% short interest with 6.6 days to cover and a call-bid skew, so finding 3 moved from -1.5 to -1.2 and finding 6 from -1.0 to -0.8.
The FPI reaction-history lesson was already applied in the draft (base rate rebuilt from confirmed releases), so abs_move_pct 11 and p_up 56 are unchanged.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction) left the findings standing: this name has not sold its good quarters; Q3 2025, the recovery analog, rose more than 11%.
